topics.label: Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and introduces the complement system as the subject of the lecture.

topics.label: Overview of Complement and C3 Function
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts of the complement cascade, its nomenclature, and the central role of C3 cleavage.

topics.label: Complement Activation Pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three distinct upstream recognition pathways that generate surface-bound convertases to activate C3.

topics.label: Effector Functions of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream immune mechanisms executed by activated complement components to destroy pathogens.

topics.label: Regulation of Complement and Host Protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins that protect host cells from accidental complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical Manifestations of Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the distinct disease presentations and clinical consequences associated with deficiencies across different complement proteins.

topics.label: Pathogen Evasion of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the evolutionary strategies pathogens use to circumvent complement activity, highlighting Staphylococcus aureus and related biomedical applications.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the presentation and announces the next lecture topic.
